findings.claim: split_pattern_segments treats a backslash before '/' as an escaped slash and does not split there, but compile_segment then treats that backslash as an escape for the following '/' and emits a literal '/' token; this can make a pattern segment contain a literal '/' and violate the spec that segments are separated by unescaped '/' outside sets.

split_pattern_segments preserves backslashes inside character classes, but compile_segment's class parser does not treat backslash specially and may interpret sequences like '\\-z' as a range or literal backslash in ways that are not clearly specified; more importantly, a backslash immediately before the closing ']' inside a class is not handled as a literal member and can cause incorrect class termination or membership.

compile_segment's range detection uses 'i + 2 < n' and 'segment[i + 2] != "]"', which incorrectly treats a dash followed by the closing bracket as a literal dash only when the dash is the last character before ']', but it can misparse ranges where the end character is ']' in other contexts and does not explicitly enforce that '-' first or last is literal in all cases.

compile_segment silently converts an invalid range with start > end into three literal members instead of raising or handling it according to the spec; this may accept patterns that should be invalid or produce unexpected matches.

match_segment only remembers the most recent star and backtracks only that star; this can be incorrect for patterns with multiple non-consecutive stars where an earlier star must be re-expanded after a later star has already consumed text, potentially causing false negatives.

The top-level DP treats a pattern segment of exactly '**' as matching zero or more whole path segments, but it does not correctly handle patterns with leading or trailing slashes or empty path segments in all cases; for example, pattern '/a' or 'a/' may not match the intended relative paths because path.split('/') and the DP alignment do not normalize empty segments consistently.

The DP for non-'**' segments only advances from dp[j] to new_dp[j+1] when j < len(path_segments), so a pattern with more segments than the path can never match, but it also does not allow a final empty pattern segment to match an empty trailing path segment unless the path string explicitly ends with '/', which may be inconsistent with whole-path matching expectations.

split_pattern_segments raises ValueError for an unterminated '[' only after scanning to the end of the entire pattern, so an unterminated class that contains an unescaped '/' is not detected at the '/' boundary and may be mis-split or produce a different error than specified.

compile_segment collapses consecutive '*' tokens into a single star, which is semantically equivalent for a single segment but conflicts with the docstring's explicit statement that elsewhere '**' is just two '*' and may hide pattern-length or edge-case expectations in hidden tests.

match_class rejects '/' for negated classes, which matches the spec, but it does so before checking membership; if a hidden test expects [!...] to match '/' when '/' is not in the set (a common glob interpretation), this will fail.
